about: Every pending pre-registered read, one entry each (section 163). scripts/due-triggers.mjs lists an entry as DUE from its `due` date until `done` is set, however overdue; the daily maintenance session performs every DUE read exactly as its registration says, records the result in docs/BACKLOG.md and the changelog, then sets `done` (the date) or moves `due` to the next check with the reason in `note`. Entries with owner `app` are carried out by the running app itself (src/main/ladder/registeredReads.ts) and are listed here so nothing is invisible.

reads.rule: backlog 227: frequent old-style fills with a band clear of zero -> add the list-price condition to leadLag.ts and take 217 to the operator; otherwise keep 1 contract and stop analysing
reads.action: code change on a pass
reads.note: 2026-09-25: FAIL on both legs of the rule. 14,763 shadow rows since 2026-09-22T18:02Z over 1,453 settled tickers. The OLD list-price mechanism (list gap >= 4c, IOC at list + 1c) fires 6,953 times and would have filled 97 - a 1% fill rate, which is not 'frequent' - at +2.5 +/- 8.9c/contract, a band that spans zero. The live mechanism (gap >= 6c net of fee) fires 59 times at +6.5 +/- 12.0c. 17 tickers/sides overlap, 80 are old-only and 42 new-only. No list-price condition is added to leadLag.ts and 217 is not taken to the operator; lead-lag stays at one contract and this line stops being analysed.

reads.note: 2026-09-25, and it answers 217 in the same direction as 227. Settlement basis: 1,958 matched windows over 3 days, Kalshi and Polymarket agree on 1,938 and disagree on 20 (1.02%); of our own 101 windows, 6 disagreed. Every disagreement landed within 4.6bp of the strike, so the basis cost is concentrated exactly where a sweep has no margin. By cell: the registered gate cell (mtc<3 and dist<5bp) is +9.13c/contract over 46 fills, 3 days, day-clustered 95% [+4.76, +13.50] - the fills a gate would refuse are the PROFITABLE ones (gated +$3.41 against kept -$2.95), so no gate is added, in either direction. With 227 failing, size above one contract has nothing supporting it: 217 stays at 1.
